title: A note answering question 2 prints answer to 1
what: 28 Oct, 02:26 UTC: an answer note with `to = [2]` on principle-lower-the-cost-of-a-failure-not-avoid printed "noted ... (answer to 1)". The note landed on question 2 correctly; the message prints the count of targets (lib/relay_queue.py:1692, f"answer to {len(targets)}"), which reads as "answer to question 1".
why: The front pastes what relay prints; a message naming the wrong question makes it believe the answer went to the wrong place (it cost one extra check today).
pass_cases: A note with `to = [2]` prints the question it answered, for example "(answer to question 2: <its title>)".
A note with `to = [1, 2]` names both questions.
